question: A car covers three different segments of a journey: it travels 40 km at a speed of 60 km/hr, then 50 km at a speed of 50 km/hr and finally 60 km at a speed of 40 km/hr. What is the car's average speed (rounded off to one decimal place) for the entire trip?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Total distance = 40 + 50 + 60 = 150 km

Total time = 40/60 + 50/50 + 60/40

= 2/3 + 1 + 3/2 = 19/6 hr

Avg speed = 150 ÷ (19/6) = 900/19 ≈ 47.4 km/hr

**∴ Answer = 47.4 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distances = 40 km, 50 km, 60 km; Speeds = 60, 50, 40 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 40 + 50 + 60 = 150 km

⇒ Time₁ = 40/60 = 2/3 hr

⇒ Time₂ = 50/50 = 1 hr

⇒ Time₃ = 60/40 = 3/2 hr

⇒ Total time = 2/3 + 1 + 3/2 = 19/6 hr

⇒ Average speed = 150 ÷ (19/6)

⇒ = 150 × 6/19 = 900/19 ≈ 47.4 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 47.4 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Key Point

Do not take simple average of speeds unless time is equal

Fraction Handling

Convert times into fractions for accuracy

Rounding

Round final answer to one decimal place
